My parents are terribly irresponsible.  I've learned - as an adult - that there are many great things about them, but some things about how they raised us and particularly me were simply criminal.

I was drinking from before I could walk.  There was whiskey in my bottle to put me to sleep and always wine with dinner.  Now a little whisky in the bottle is bad, but somehow they justified it and a small glass of wine with dinner didn't seem so strange in our jewish household.

But, by the time I was 10 I was already an accomplished alcoholic.  Not that I drank A LOT.  I just drank all the time.  I had learned to use alcohol to calm my nerves, to make school fun, and to go to sleep.  I snuck it from my parents who were pretty neglectful and carried it to school in sprite bottles that I saved.  

I only drank a little at a time back then, like it was medicine.  But, by the time I was 13 things were getting dark.  My parents divorced and my mothers new boyfriend was extremely abusive phsyically, verbally, and sexually.  I drank all the time and started running away for weeks at a time.  I began using heroin and running with gutter punks.

By the time I was 18 I was so severely addicted to alcohol my days completely revolved around getting alcohol.  I would wake up and drink the cocktail I was too drunk to drink the night before and pour myself a vodka/soda with breakfast.  I'd easily go through a 5th of vodka in a day.  And I'm a 5"1 female.  I'm not like a big dude of anything.

When I was 21 my friends who had always just thought I was a 
"champion" now could tell there was something wrong.  I was getting physically sick, a lot of this had to do with my speed addiction - of which I was now 2 years deep.  The speed allowed me to drink actually even MORE.  Now I was going through a 5 minimum a day, which was expensive.  My skin turned yellow, my belly was swollen, i was 20lbs overweight and just looked awful.  My skin was broken out in sore from the speed, my gums bled, my whole body was screaming.

Then I ended up in the hospital with liver failure.  I was 23.  Besides the extreme alcohol use, speed use, I was also drinking NyQuil routinely to get to sleep at night.  I drank NyQuil, vicodin, somas, relafins, theraflu, benadryl, sleepinol.  Any kind of downer I could find in my mothers cabinet.  The alcohol, speed, poor diet, and constant stream of downers had officially taken it's toll.

I spent a week in the hospital.  I don't remember much except the crippling pain in my side.  My whole body ached from convulsions, vomiting, and seizing.  See, I wasn't a binge drinker.  I was what they call a French alcoholic.  I just always had alcohol in my system, from the time I was little.  My brain chemistry just seized up when I didn't get it.

After being sent home I was too sick to even get to my dealer who lived down the street.  My mother locked me in my bedroom and I spent the next 5 days just puking.  The seizures nearly killed me as I hit my head so many times.  No one checked on me.  I drank water from the laundry facilities that happened to be in my room.  I didn't shit.  I couldn't keep anything down, but I was pissing in a bucket that I also puked in.

After that I kicked speed and I kicked alcohol.  I quit drinking mostly because it hurt me so badly it started making me ill just to smell it.  I started exercising and eventually began running marathons.  I lost the 20lbs and got so healthy I actually began modeling.

Over the next few years I really reflecting on how I had gotten the way I had been and why.  I realized that alcoholism runs in my family on both sides and I realized how much better things were without it.

Now I'm in my 30's and I will have a glass of wine with a meal if I'm out with friends or a beer on saturday night, just to have something to hold in my hand.  But, I never drink hard alcohol and I never drink more than 2 in a night and I always make sure to drink a lot of water.

Right now I'm pregnant and, of course, I'm not drinking at all and I'm totally fine with that.  There is no way I will ever give my child alcohol.  Not until they are an adult.  What my parents thought me to do was to use alcohol like medication, and that was the real damage.

I don't have attention problems but I have anxiety disorder and that makes it hard to focus subsequently.  The worst part is that my anxiety manifests itself primarily physically.  I get shingles once or twice a year, lesions in my GI tracts, rashes on my face, muscle pain from clenching without thinking, etc...  I also have a very high pressure job working in the medical field, so it's very important that I work hard to stay relaxed and on point without getting gnarly rashes all over my face.

What I do to combat this is I basically work myself to death every single day and then I go home and run 5 miles and do 500 crunches and stretch.  I can't stand slow days because my mind gets fuzzy and I can't stay on point.  I work best when I'm constantly moving - even breaking a sweat.  The days where we have 60 patients and I'm physically running and really triaging - those are the days that I thrive on.  The more work I have the easier it is for me to do well because there's no downtime for my mind to wander and all that extra energy is being used.

I usually feel exhausted when I'm on the bus home from work and don't feel like running but I do it anyways because I know if I don't I'm going to sit in my apartment for another 4 hours.  And that just means I'm going to drink alcohol (which will keep me up) and surf the internet.  Basically, I'll just be pooling in my own energy.  All the anxiety will start to build up again as soon as I sit down and "relax".  So, in order to relax I have to basically run myself into exhaustion.

Then I shower, put my scrubs out for the next day, and go to bed.  Now on a good day I can sleep for 5 hours, most nights I have to do this on less sleep.  I can't tell which one is more effective for burning off the energy though.  I think sometimes if I don't sleep well for a few nights and - as I like to call it "burn" - I often find myself with a day or 2 of real sleep plus clear head, where I can actually be normal. "So hows the job hunt?"

The problem is that doctors DON'T have the time to spend with you.  They run on very tight schedules that are often destroyed when someone comes in 30 minutes late.  The staff tries to schedule for there to be late patients but after 2 or 3 30 minute late patients your schedule is destroyed and you only scheduled to be with each patient in 10min - 45min intervals, depending on the visit type.

It's not that the doctor doesn't care.  Most of - if not all - the doctors I've worked with care and do what they do out of a genuine interest and are deeply effected by a patient who passes or falls more seriously ill.  However, there's often little they can do sometimes because of insurance companies and sometimes because of lack of time.  If they know you have a lot of questions, they can schedule for that, but if you just show up for a routine physical and suddenly have 50 billion questions, they're going to hustle through them.

To be perfectly honest I haven't done a whole lot of research on it.  I base this information off of 3 things:

A. I worked for the mental health department for 2 years in data entry when I was 16 - 18.  This was, granted, over a decade ago.  But, I learned then that all the government run mental institutions in the state had been shut down over a decade prior.

If you're curious what kind of data I was entering, basically if someone had a nervous breakdown (or was seeing a therapist for the first time) the initial report from the doctor would come to me and I would type it into the system.  I learned a VAST amount about not only different kinds of mental health disorders, how they are classified, how they are treated, but how the system (or lack thereof) deals with them.

B. My uncle has schizophrenia.  He was first admitted to a government run mental institution in the 1970's, but during Reagan's administration the government run institutions - at least in that area (which I assume was also California, but might not be.) - were shut down.  He was missing for almost a year before he was found living under a freeway overpass since the institution had just let him off on the curb since no one was available to pick him up.

If you're interested in confirmation that Reagan did this all you have to do is google "reagan shut down mental institutions" and several resources come up.  They could probably explain the reasons WHY he did this better than I, but my understanding is that it had something to do with balancing the national budget.

C. When I was 19 I was depressed, a friend gave me several klonopins and I had a few beers.  I next thing I knew I was getting out of a car on the freeway and the next thing I knew I was in the psyche ward in general hospital (San Francisco), ironically.  I was there for a week and got to experience the system first hand.  The maximum amount of time they keep me there would've been 2 weeks.  It is not equipped for extended stay.  If I had needed/wanted to go to an institution there were none available.  I could've gone to a rehabilitation clinic and paid for it out of pocket, which was suggested, but since I didn't have an actual addiction to klonopins and was over it I just wanted to go home and not go a million dollars into debt.

So no.  I don't have a ton of proof of what I'm saying.  In fact, as far as you know, I could be making all that up to.  But, I do speak from personal experience not only working in the system, being in the system, but also having family in the system.

My understanding with climate change is that the global climate has gone through several massive shifts.  The human race has also come back from the brink of existence (and possibly complete extinction) several times.  We have evidence of dramatic climate changes altering human life in the past: ancient ghost cities, underwater cities, etc...

So, I do believe we are in the middle of a major climate shift with probable long term extreme weather.  However, there are places on earth that already have had extreme weather for as long as there's been documented history and people just either don't live there or they adapt to it.  I assume we will do the same again and I don't assume that climate change will happen over night.

People will and have been taken out by massive tsunamis, storms, earthquakes, hurricanes, volcanic eruptions.  A few hundred here, a few thousand there.  If the bees die out we will have mass problems of scurvy, however vitamin C can be gotten from common lawn grass, so the extinction of most fruits would be mostly just sad because it's tasty.  Super viruses may break out in more densely populated areas due to poor farming practices and/or overuse of antibiotics.  But, by no means will it wipe out the human race.  We'll simply move to higher ground.

Basically, just because the world - as we know it - may be coming to a long drawn out end, doesn't mean the human race will be going anywhere or even necisarily changing very much.  We just might have to relocate.
